headline: City Council votes 5-3 to deny Pawtucket Teachers' Alliance contract for 2026 through 2029
summary: The three-year contract runs from September 1st, 2026 through August 31st, 2029. The superintendent shared a summary of a state projection showing a possible $10 million to $15 million cut in state aid for fiscal 2028. Wendy's request to stay open until 4:00 a.m. at 120 Broad Street was also denied. A tax stabilization agreement for 30 Beatrice Street was recommended.
decisions: Approved a tax abatement for April, May, and June 2026 totaling $22,312.67, 3-0.
Approved a tax abatement for July through September 2026 totaling $152,458.08, 3-0.
Finance Committee recommended denial of the teachers' contract, 2-1.
Denied the teachers' contract, 5-3, following the Finance Committee's recommendation.
Recommended the tax stabilization agreement for 30 Beatrice Street, 3-0.
Recommended adoption of an ordinance setting pay rates for the finance and grant compliance officer, 3-0.
Denied Wendy's request to stay open until 4:00 a.m. at 120 Broad Street.
Approved a Class B liquor license for Morning Sunshine Cafe at 176 Columbus Avenue.
Approved the Class A liquor license renewal for Stateline Wine & Spirits at 880 Central Avenue.
discussion: Teachers' contract cost: Members questioned whether years two and three could be funded, and the superintendent's summary of a state projection raised new budget concerns.
Teachers' contract public comment: Speakers, including teachers and parents, urged approval, citing pay, class sizes, and working without a contract since September.
Wendy's late hours: Members questioned how extra hours would affect nearby residents and asked for police logs. The applicant said most customers are local.
Pinecrest traffic: Residents asked for speed bumps, one-way streets, and better crosswalks on Rice Street and Weldon Street, saying cars move too fast.
